name: Mirtazapine
drug_class: Noradrenergic and specific serotonergic antidepressant (NaSSA); tetracyclic
route_note: Oral tablets or orally disintegrating tablets once daily, usually at bedtime.

discovery.note: An aza-analogue of the tetracyclic antidepressant mianserin, developed at Organon in the Netherlands.

tagline: Sedating tetracyclic antidepressant that blocks alpha-2 and several serotonin receptors
summary: Mirtazapine is a tetracyclic antidepressant that increases noradrenaline and serotonin release by blocking presynaptic alpha-2 receptors. Its potent antihistamine effect makes it sedating and appetite-stimulating, and it causes little sexual dysfunction or nausea.
mechanism: Mirtazapine antagonises presynaptic alpha-2 adrenergic autoreceptors and heteroreceptors, disinhibiting the release of noradrenaline and serotonin. Concurrent blockade of 5-HT2 and 5-HT3 receptors channels the serotonergic effect towards 5-HT1A receptors.
Potent histamine H1 antagonism causes sedation, particularly at lower doses, and increased appetite and weight gain.

history.title: First approval
history.detail: Mirtazapine is approved in the Netherlands.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: The FDA approves Remeron for depression.

history.title: Generics
history.detail: Generic mirtazapine becomes available in the US.

history.title: Suicidality warning
history.detail: Class boxed warning on suicidality in young people.

history.title: Organon spin-off
history.detail: Remeron moves to Organon & Co. when it is spun off from Merck.

safety.boxed_warning: Increased risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviours in children, adolescents and young adults (under 25) taking antidepressants; monitor for clinical worsening.

facts: Mirtazapine is often chosen where insomnia, poor appetite or SSRI-induced sexual dysfunction are concerns.
